$comment: Copy to <repo>/.claude/catchup.config.json and delete what you don't need. Every field is optional — the skill works with no config at all.

authors.$comment: Turn split on only for a repo with more than one real contributor. Every commit email must be listed, or it lands in unknown_authors.

categories.$comment: paths/keywords EXTEND the built-in rules. Use paths_replace/keywords_replace to discard them instead. Titles are yours to change; the three keys are not.

summary.$comment: Raise these for a repo that routinely runs hundreds of commits a week.

ignore.$comment: Bookkeeping commits — excluded from counts but always reported as a number. These EXTEND the built-ins (.claude/transcripts, lockfiles, chore(transcripts): ...).

deepvista.$comment: Sync entities to DeepVista context cards over the hosted MCP server. Off by default.

card_types.$comment: Override the entity-type -> DeepVista card_type mapping. Values must be DeepVista's own card types.

subjects.$comment: What this repo produces evidence ABOUT, and where that evidence lives. Only meaningful for a repo that evaluates or researches things outside itself; omit it entirely otherwise. Without it the altitude rule is unenforceable — a commit log describes what changed in the repo, and only these artifacts describe the thing being studied, so a learning drifts into being about a defect in the tooling instead of about the subject.
subjects.noun: the thing this repo studies — e.g. a technology, a company, a customer
subjects.read_first: The summary or headline field those artifacts carry — someone's considered one-sentence answer, written with the whole subject in front of them.

method_notes.$comment: Where this repo keeps what it has learned about running its own catchups: which themes recur, which past summary went wrong and why. Lives beside the output rather than inside the skill, so the skill stays portable and the hard-won specifics stay with the repo.

git.$comment: Off by default — catchups are working artifacts and landing them is the user's call.

learnings.$comment: Optional. Omit and the skill uses its generic ladder: asserted / reported / observed / verified / measured. Override only if your repo already grades evidence in its own words, so the catchup uses the same scale as everything else you write.

themes.$comment: Optional. What share of a week's commits a candidate theme must carry to lead the summary. A repo of many tiny commits and one of few large ones do not agree about what 15% means.
